Данная игра представляет собой интересный синтез элементов, присущих популярным мобильным платформам, таким как Doodle Jump, с уникальными характеристиками, характерными для жанра roguelike, а также системой постепенного улучшения игровых параметров. Это позволяет отнести её к категории казуальных игр, способствующих эффективному использованию времени и предоставляющих пользователю возможность активного взаимодействия с виртуальным пространством.

С точки зрения технического исполнения, игра отличается высоким уровнем качества, что проявляется в детально проработанной графике, интуитивно понятном интерфейсе и сбалансированной системе игрового процесса. Основная механика игры заключается в необходимости постоянного восхождения по уровням, каждый из которых завершается столкновением с боссом, что добавляет элемент динамики и стратегического планирования.

Одной из ключевых особенностей данной игры является её нелинейная структура, позволяющая игрокам выбирать различные пути развития и адаптироваться к изменяющимся условиям. Кроме того, возможность совместного прохождения добавляет дополнительный уровень социального взаимодействия и повышает реиграбельность.

Таким образом, данная игра представляет собой достойный образец цифровых развлечений, сочетающий в себе элементы различных жанров и предлагающий игрокам уникальный опыт взаимодействия в виртуальной среде.

Avalanche 2: Super Avalanche, bağımlılık yaratan oynanışıyla ödüller kazanan hızlı tempolu bir arcade platform oyunudur. Oyuncular, yükselen lav, ejderhalar ve uzay tavukları gibi engellerden kaçarken düşen bloklara tırmanırken zıplayan bir hatmi karakterini kontrol eder. Oyun, tamamlanması gereken görevler ve mücadeleler içeren tek oyunculu bir modun yanı sıra daha da kaotik bir oynanış için son derece eğlenceli bir kooperatif moduna sahiptir.

Avalanche 2'nin güçlü yanlarından biri, basit kontrolleri sayesinde sıradan oyunculardan aşırı rekabetçi oyunculara kadar tüm oyuncular için erişilebilir olmasıdır. Oyuncular düşen dükkanlardan güçlendiriciler satın alabilir, görevler toplayabilir ve oyunu değiştiren yükseltmeler satın almak için paralarını bankaya yatırabilirler. Oyun, kilidini açmak için 100.000'den fazla güçlendirici, rozet ve kostüm kombinasyonu sunuyor.

Yüksek kaliteli müzik parçaları oyunun genel deneyimine katkıda bulunur. Avalanche 2, çok fazla derinlik ve tekrar oynanabilirlik sunan eğlenceli ve zorlu bir arcade platform oyunudur, bu da onu hızlı tempolu ve bağımlılık yapıcı bir oyun deneyimi arayan oyuncular için mükemmel bir seçim haline getirir.

This has to be one of the most underrated games on steam. I first played this back in 2015 because northernlion did a video on this. I recently returned to the game to get every single achievement and it has been a blast back then and still is today.

It is such a simple game, your only goal is to climb as high as you can. However falling blocks, hordes of enemies and bosses make your life hard. To help you on your journey to the top the game provides plenty of varied powerups, most of them improve your mobility but there are also defensive and economy based powerups and of course familiars.

The best part about the game is how good the movement feels, at first you start out a little slow and clumsy but as you keep climbing and get some meta-unlocks you eventually start soaring through the air moreso than jumping from block to block. The game rewards you for a risky playstyle, if you combo-kill enemies and surf on platforms you get more coins and as a result of that you can afford more powerups which leads to better runs.

Getting 100% achievements in this game is fun, the only annoying achievement is to get burned by lava 50 times which means you have to die intentionally for about 10 minutes to unlock it.

weirdly, this is a sequel to a flash game that i played way too much of in high school, which is how it made it onto my steam wishlist. it left such a weak impression on me that it stayed there for years, probably longer than any other game on there now, until a desperate fit of procrastination convinced me that it was worth paying a few bucks for. 

it's shockingly fun, and i wish i had picked it up earlier!

it leaves a miserable first impression - it's got possibly the worst UX of any game i've played in ages and when you first start playing it feels absolutely terrible, straight garbage. it's even got occasional collision problems which is normally a complete dealbreaker for a platformer... but it's got just a couple extra mechanics (an absurdly high bounce-off-enemies-by-holding-jump, and a fastfall), plus some fun movement powerups, which take playing it from garbage to insta-flow state basically immediately. the skill curve goes from trash to really fun, precise, high APM platforming in an extremely short amount of time. it's not a long game, definitely the easiest roguelite i've ever played, but the core is solid. 

i call it a roguelite rather than an arcade game 'cause on top of the fun take on platforming, it has a thoughtful and satisfying meta-progression system where you collect optional objectives and choose which you want to bring with you into a run. you "level up" to unlock new powerups but it's almost like a formality, it takes very little time to max level and is more a way of introducing trickier powerups slightly later. reminds me a bit of super crate box here. it also has a surprisingly deep load out system where you can start with various powerups for various penalties, and there's enough different mix and matching to make different builds feel different to play. this also complements the optional objectives well cause you can build heavily around completing certain objectives. again, the UI for picking objectives and missions is garbage, but that comes with old indie territory. 

it borrows liberally from other roguelites, most notably spelunky (shortcuts, teleporter/jetpack as late game high skill cap items, snakes that are way more annoying than they should be) but it all fits together into a cohesive package. the most generous way i could describe it is "spelunky but upwards" (or maybe "downwell but upwards?"), and though it's honestly not as thoughtful, cohesive, or polished as either of them, if you feel like wall jumps, fast falls, bouncing off enemies, and quick decision making wrapped up in the lightest of roguelite metaprogressions, it's well worth a few bucks.

I was actually reluctant to buy this considering how little attention it was getting as silly as it sounds, because the trailer was trying too hard to do the adult swim anti-humour bit and didn't show too much gameplay. I thought since that only a total of 28 people have reviewed it (upon time of buying) that it was just a small forgettable indie game that didn't have much lasting appeal or grabbing power. I finally bought it on sale, yet I would recommend it full price.

The music and graphics for this game are the first thing that stand out- catchy and gorgeous. The gameplay's grasp on you as the player probably won't be immediate though... I started out the game frustrated and bored. The tutorial only gives you the basics (which is enough, although it doesn't have any music for some reason, making me worry the rest of the game would be just as silent) and after that you're thrown into the game, which is painfully slow to start off. The game will also be shockingly hard when you first start playing as well, making every death a "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, do I really have to start over from the slow bit again?".

The gameplay summed up shortly: It's that one level from yoshi's island where you have to vertically climb a tower of falling blocks, only it's the entire game with much more depth. When you first start out, you will get squished. Many times. The lava will probably never kill you, because it starts out slow as molasses unless you get the risk badge. You will never be able to actually land on those damn birds that fly at you, and sometimes you might be able to sneak in a snake kill, but more often than not you'll miscalculate your jump and land right beside them, killing you instantly. Manage to get to the first boss? It will be a tedious test of patience until you finally start to do some risky moves, which will in turn make you end up dead and sending you down to the bottom again.

Yes, this game isn't a forgiving teacher. But don't hit that refund button just yet- it gets better. I got a hang of the game surprisingly fast, and it's secret amount of depth blindsided me. You'll start learning how to surf, and how to get combos to squeeze out as many coins as possible. You'll actually start to remember that the screen wraps and learn how to use it to your advantage. You'll learn how to kill the bosses quickly. You might even make it to space, or the moon once or twice.

I do have some minor complaints with the game though, but nothing gamebreaking. Sometimes you can get an absolute terrible roll of RNG where blocks just do not stack at all how you want them to and it just never ends, making you die after a good run or make you restart at the beginning of one so you can actually progress. Walljumping feels responsive most of the times, but sometimes when you're trying to chain it, it's the most frustrating thing in the world. And for the love of god, I hate how shops work. I'm trying to run up away from the advancing wall of death and I accidentally jump on one of the shop chests, wasting my money. And if it's a deposit/withdrawl chest, I might hit my head on a ceiling and deposit multiple times. I would gladly rather press an action button to buy something than have to jump on it, even if it's some sort of badge that I have to equip to balance it out. Also, some challenges are lamely bugged, allowing you to cheat- the chest one in particular, you can just use a bank over and over to cheat it rather than actually get chests in one run.

I'm not sure how long this game is before looping, and I'm not sure if the flash game was just as good as this, but I'd say those things aside it's absolutely worth your money. If you're on the fence, maybe wait on sale, but otherwise you won't regret full price.

I was a big fan of the original Avalanche flash game many many years ago, but as time went on and flash games went out of style, I forgot about the game entirely. Then when browsing steam, I all of a sudden came across its sequel, not knowing anything about it, and decided to try it on a whim.

This game is the definition of a perfect sequel. The core gameplay from the original game which made it fun is still the focal point, just improved, and every gripe I had with the first game has been fixed. The gameplay, which consists of going as high as possible, is addictive with missions and items keeping it fresh and interesting, even after the amount of time I've already spent on the game. You can tell there was a large focus on making the gameplay feel smooth. The controls feel very similar to the way super meatboy feels, which is to say good. The graphics and music compliment the game quite well, both being very well made and a pleasure to see/hear, and overall the presentation is great, with intuitive menus and nothing to bog you down between games. 

Some people may argue on the price point, which is a fair point to argue given the amount of breathtaking games on steam available for the same price, but as the guy's first game on steam I could see where he is coming from. I really enjoy it, so if you don't mind the price, or the game is on sale, I'd definitely recommend trying it out.
